species: Schizachyrium scoparium (little bluestem; species modelled, cultivars noted only)
note: DRAFT written 2026-11-27 by a research agent from the sources listed; nothing has been built or measured, so these ranges are not tuned to any build. Each check says whether its numbers are sourced, an owner decision, an estimate from photographs, or a tolerance. This is a GRASS: the ratibida checks for bloom weeks (bloom-p10, bloom-p50, bloom-end, bloom-end-sourced, bloom-correlation), head-fraction and first-year-leaf are removed because they do not fit (iNaturalist's Flowers annotation has 4 Ohio records, a grass has no bloom end, and a plug's blades sprawl rather than point up). Checks whose type does not exist yet in the gate's TYPES table are marked needsNewType and are advisory until code exists. 'stems' in params means culms (flowering stems) and 'seedHeads' means culms carrying raceme fluff; the orchestrator maps them in stats. Height means culm-tip height; leaf mound height is its own check. Culm counts are estimates from photographs (no source gives a number), so every culm check is advisory except the cap and the winter presence check, both widened. Age 0 is a plug; a division from Karen's Pollinator Garden is not a plug and its starting age is an owner decision. Converted for the gate 27 Nov 2026: grass checks culmEmergence, seedFluff and cutback use stats only; culmMoundRatio needs the plant to expose _snapshot leaves and axes. Starting age is 0 (seed-grown), no division. Ranges still need the owner's approval at plan review.

bloomData.note: iNaturalist's Flowers annotation has only 4 Ohio records, so there is no usable weekly bloom curve and bloomPercentile / bloomEnd / bloomCorrelation are not proposed. The all-observation curve is when people photograph the plant (mostly seed heads and fall colour). Weekly sum 497, API total 505, which disagree by 8; for 2021-2025 sum 271 equals API total 271. Week numbers use iNaturalist's week_of_year and may differ by one from floor((day-1)/7)+1.

visual: Plug (age 0): about 12 bright yellow-green blades from 2 to 4 tillers, sprawling and arching, longest blade roughly 8 in (judged against about 1 in mulch pieces), no culms (Stow OH, 2026-05-09). Seed-grown juvenile at 8 weeks (NRCS seedling guide, PDF page 31): about 4 thin blades, tallest about 4.5 in.

Mature mound: blue-green to grey-green blades with purple-tinged bases, folded, pointed, arching in a fountain; mound about 30 to 45 percent of culm-tip height; culms rise from the centre and flare, leaning in different directions at the tips.

Culms: thin, flattened, yellow to reddish-brown with red nodes (UIUC), branching only toward the tip into paired racemes 1 to 3 in long that are pink-purple, then silvery white and feathery; fluff along the upper half of each culm in September (West Lafayette, Akron).
Fall: culms red-purple and blades burgundy to purple-red late October (Delaware OH), copper through November, copper-orange standing in January (Beavercreek OH).
Spring: old stand is tan; fresh bright green shoots seen 21 April in Cincinnati; leaf mound complete by late June.
Not viewed: flower head from above; close bloom stage with anthers. Culm counts are estimates read from photographs, not counts.

Judged by eye (no gate check yet): blade length 8 to 12 in and width 1.5 to 6 mm; a plug's blades sprawl, about 12 of them in spring; crown 0.25 to 0.5 and top 0.45 to 0.85 of the culm height in width; colour blue-green to grey-green with a purple base in summer, copper to burgundy from about day 265, tan to copper in winter.
